utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, yesterday we also discussed the fact that how many witnesses you had referred to or you had had contact with, and your answer today was similar as what you informed me yesterday, and that there was only one witness statement that you had consulted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Are you referring to this particular incident --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: -- Maljine? At that time, yes, it was just one eyewitness to the incident that I've consulted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, I would just like to refer to -- again, the notes compiled by you and Thomas Osorio, where it says that -- and it says: "Immediately before the soldiers opened fire, a loud cry was heard. In this, the witness testimony differs from another one, (redacted), see below, told that the prisoners were lined up against the fence and that the shooting started upon explicit command." When, if ever, did you meet witness (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can't remember talking to a witness called (redacted) or to anybody else who would present him or herself as an eyewitness to this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So the information -- did you receive any information, any statement or report by witness (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can't remember. Thomas though might have had some separate information obtained from elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, during that first interview, I would like to confirm that what my colleague referred to, and that was that a map was -- or a sketch was done. I would like to show you a sketch. And I have sufficient copies for everyone. Witness ZO, do you recognise this sketch? I don't know if you were shown your statement by my colleague, but do you recognise this sketch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: It's the first time I see it in -- after 11 years. I recognise it. That's the sketch which had been sketched in front of us. In front of me and Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this sketch, Witness ZO, was taken back with you to Zagreb, but is it possible that it was left behind as an indication to Randy Rhodes or to someone else within the British Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: The original, I'm sure, had been taken back to Zagreb. A copy of an indication could have been left with the British Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness ZO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like this document to be admitted, because it was recognised by the witness. This sketch was given to him by the person that he interviewed with regard to the events in Maljine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH177.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, concerning this interview with this witness, I would just like to recall some of the events as they were mentioned to you by him, if you recall, Witness ZO, that there were Mr. Berislav or Marjanovic -- do you recall this name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was escorted by 80 to 100 soldiers and he met a group of 18 prisoners of war, one of which -- one of whom was injured.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I remember that this was his story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he mentioned to you that the prisoner of war were guarded by people who were wearing masks and that did not speak the language and that they were dressed both in civilian and military clothes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: As far as I remember, that was what has been told -- what we've been told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that the person who was wearing a mask selected 18 from his group including Marjanovic, and told them to join the group of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct. That's my recollection about this interview -- or coincide with what you're telling -- with what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that these people who were selected, according to the notes I have, were 12 males of a young age -- or 12 fit males.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I'm sure that you're reading our report correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that he said that when they were taken out by the people wearing those masks, he heard a loud cry. Then somehow they opened fire. He was shot in the leg and he escaped.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is that basically what he told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That's basically the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this (redacted) that you don't know about, are you aware that he had a different story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I'm not aware about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, at that time you did not take any further action with respect to this incident, after the interview.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Apart from filing our report to Geneva, not any immediate action had been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You did not go and see 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In fact, you -- maybe you did not even know it was 3 Corps. You knew that maybe they were a Muslim army but not 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: You're very much correct in assessing the level of my competence at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And back in Zagreb more information came in which led you to believe that maybe something really happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: We have shared our opinions with Thomas after that interview, and our conclusion was that that witness was trustworthy, so any additional information which we received in Zagreb added to the primary information which we received, and that was the eyewitness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, in this report that was given to us as part of background information, at the end there is a Note 1, which reads: "In addition to our previous note, we would like to suggest that in view of the fact that local HDZ and HVO people messed up with the alleged execution and since considerable time has elapsed since then, the most reliable way to verify the testimony would be to interview those civilians who were in the first group escorted from Maljine, and who might have witnessed the moment of selection of the 12 men to join the group of prisoners of war. There are indications of where these persons might be." Do you recall this note being added to your report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that this means that there was actually a second report drawn about the same incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: The way I would read that report is that we suggested some follow-up action, but I cannot recall whether this suggestion and proposal of ours had in fact been followed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you did not follow up yourself with interviewing those people, or you don't know of anyone who did so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No, we did not ourselves didn't try to trace them, and I don't know of any attempt by anybody to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, in Zagreb, you also received more information. And I'd like to refer you to also another piece of information which was given to us as background information, and this is another witness testimony. It's dated 26th of June, and it says: "Please find enclosed a tape on which was recorded the testimony of an eyewitness of a war crime in Maljine. Also enclosed is a summary of the statement prepared by" -- I will not mention the name -- "MP at BH command who heard the witness on 25 June." Do you recall receiving this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall that in this information was also a different story from the first two you had received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't recall differences.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And is it possible that this man here actually mentioned to you that he tried to escape and that when trying to escape, that's when fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this -- actually, this statement here also contains -- and I think I will -- I should maybe show it to you, with the consent of my colleague. I don't intend to produce it, but it is background information that was given to us. With the consent of the Chamber and of my colleague, I would like to show it to you, because it says here that after -- well, at least that this witness says that the people who were dead were picked up in a truck and taken away. I just read this quote, and I will maybe show you the document, where it says here: "The people who were killed, what did they do with them? Are they still over there? Are they buried? Answer: I don't know exactly. I don't know exactly what happened. Those which were on execution came with a truck to take them. But where they take them, I do not know. And what did they do with them, I do not know anything."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you agree, we could place this document on the ELMO in order to be able to see the relevant paragraph in this declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With your leave, and perhaps in light of the suggestion by Mr. Bourgon, if I could just see document before it's placed on the ELMO, I would appreciate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I may ask the -- the usher just to raise the document a bit further up so we can see the question where it says: "The people who were killed." [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like the inform you that the highlighted parts were highlighted by myself. [In English] "What did they do with them? Are they still over there? Are they buried?" [Interpretation] And then the answer appears. [In English] May I ask the usher to take the document away, please. [Interpretation] With your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Do you remember reading this statement? Because this was part of the package that was sent to Thomas Osorio on the 26th of June. Did you ever see this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I cannot remember receiving and reading this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You cannot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's move on quickly, Witness ZO. On 6th of July, you had a conversation with an ECMM monitor called Mr. Huet. Mr. Huet was an ECMM monitor in Zenica from May to June of 1993 and you had a meeting with him in Zagreb on the 6th of July. Do you recall this meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could the usher distribute a document that I would like to show the witness. The date of the document is the 6th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, may I ask you to take a look at this document and tell me if you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: It should be my report to Geneva. I sent about -- lots of them, and this would seem like my style. So I would recognise this as my document, as my report.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Now, you go on to describe the way he talked about the operation, and he mentions in this document what happens in what town. And then there's a comment from yourself at the end of the second paragraph, where you say: "Still judging by the information he obtained on killings and allegations on other villages, a number of inhabitants, mainly males of the affected villages, were summarily executed." Was that from him or from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Let me read this phrase again, and I will come up with my answer. I think this is something which is attributable to him. My -- as a general rule, I tried to indicate my opinions, my proposals, to be very -- I tried to be very specific when it's something which is attributable to me as an author of this document. I don't see such an attribution here, so I think this is something which Mr. Huet told me, and that's his assumption.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if I mention to you, Witness ZO, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it might be necessary to correct part of the transcript because one of these witnesses is a protected witness. So it might be necessary to redact part of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, could you prepare an order to redact from line 62 and 63 references made to the person mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, looking at this document, if I tell you that the two persons mentioned on this document actually testified before this Trial Chamber and never mentioned anything about these murders, would that indicate to you that the information, for whatever reason provided to you, was not reliable?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: It would be an interpretation, and what I would hold myself responsible for is the accuracy of this report on the conversation of -- my conversation with Mr. Huet. About the accuracy of his conversations, of his findings, I would not hold myself responsible for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And just one last question on this document, Witness ZO: The fact that Mr. Huet informed you that his estimation is that there was 1.000 Mujahedin from Pakistan, Iran, and Afghanistan between Zenica and Travnik, do you recall this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: If it's here, it has been provided to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would that be the type of information that would trigger in you something that -- a need to go further, because the word "Mujahedin" was mentioned and the number "1.000" was mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to tender this document into evidence. The witness has recognised the document, or at least the contents of the document. This document should be tendered confidentially, under seal, given the nature of its contents. This is a document that we obtained via electronic disclosure from the Prosecution. And in this case we believe, Mr. President, that it is a document referred to in Rule 68 - at least that is our interpretation in Rule 68 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. And it is a document that wasn't provided to the Defence -- it wasn't forwarded to the Defence. After the completion of this witness's testimony, I would like address the Chamber about this matter. For the moment, I would like to request an exhibit number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Mundis, the Defence is requesting that this document be tendered into evidence. It obtained the document through electronic means. The witness has authenticated this document, has recognised this document. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number under seal, a definitive exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit number will be DH178, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, I would like to ask you whether on the 20th of July is the date at which you sent your report to Geneva which included the newspaper article from Zagreb, which was shown to you earlier, and that was Exhibit P277. This mentions 20 July. I would like if you can confirm that this is the date that -- at which you sent the document to Geneva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't have it before me any more. If the document is dated -- and it's not a typographic mistake, then I think that is the date when the report has been sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show the witness document P277.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, do you now have the document which is P277?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't see the number P277 -- yes, now I have it. Now I've seen the number P277. This is the document, that's the report we've just been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can I ask you with the help of the usher to put this document, at least the first page, on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a problem as far as this document is concerned. It might reveal someone's identity, so we would not like it to be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, that was my mistake. I should have thought of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, can you look at this document which includes the newspaper article which you forwarded to Zagreb -- sorry, to Geneva. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This document includes a translation of the newspaper article, which in fact has been forwarded from Zagreb to Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask, Witness ZO, that you turn to the page of the document, looking at the bottom numbers, and this document -- the last -- the before-last page, and that is page 00124599.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: In my case, this is the last page of the document I'm looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The last page of the document in English. Can you, with the help of the usher, put this page on the ELMO, given that there are no information on this page that can identify. Witness ZO, can you confirm that this page, there is a report about a shooting statement on Bikosi and that is a statement that was given on the 19th of June by an eyewitness to the shooting? Can you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: The way it reads, you're absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you confirm at the last line, where it says that "this statement was received by a representative of the HDZ in the Bosnia-Herzegovina" or -- no, sorry -- "by a representative of the HDZ."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That's what I see in front of me on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that this is a fourth statement concerning this incident which also has a different story to it than the first three that we mentioned this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: What I see on the screen in front of me does not contradict the general line of the story as it had been told to me and to my colleague in the beginning of June in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the general line is the same --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I see no contradictions here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this is the fourth -- you would agree that this is the fourth statement that we look at together, even though the last one you did not recognise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I'm starting to get confused. The last one. Before that, we'd been discussing the reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- Is the one that was sent on the 26th of June to Thomas Osorio by BH command.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I think the last document we discussed was the report on my meeting with Mr. Huet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry. I'm referring to in terms of on this incident in Maljine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We showed you first, we discussed the statement based on your notes with a Mr. Marjanovic, and we discussed something concerning a 23 witness (redacted).Then we discussed something concerning a witness which was interviewed at BH command, and this one you did not recall.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I did not recall that one, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And now we're speaking about a fourth, at least, recollection of the events in Maljine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you agree that the four have the same general line but there are differences in the four?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I would rather say that there is -- I would rather repeat what I've said, that there is nothing in this -- in what I've seen in front of me which would contradict the story which had been told to us by the eyewitness to the killing. I would like also to stipulate one thing: This is the translation from an article which had been published in Vjesnik. So this is not a testimony which one of my colleagues took from anybody. This is just a translation from the article, and I had some experiences in the field when newspapers exaggerated or underreported the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness ZO. Now, can you confirm when you received this information? Because you sent it to Geneva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So when did you receive this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: When did I receive it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you confirm when or under what occasion you received this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This is easy, because the article is dated 19 July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember the person or the organisation which provided you with this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This is not the statement. Again, this is the article in the newspaper. I think we received -- we subscribed to many local newspapers, including Vjesnik, and our -- a number of our local staff was responsible for looking through them and for calling our attention to something which we should rather be informed about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness ZO. I'm sorry about my referring to a statement. It's just because if you look at -- under the heading "Shooting statement in Bikosi," that's why I referred to the word "statement." But I agree with you, it's just a recollection. And this was actually published in the paper and given to you by some media person.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No. This was published in the paper and was given to me and to my colleagues by our local staff who was responsible for monitoring of local press.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness ZO. Now, if we look at this specific statement once again for one quick look. If we look at the first line where it says: "In the village of Bikosi beside Guca Gora on 8 June 1993 in the morning they were captured by the army and -- beside Maljine and were taken to a detention centre in Mehurici." Now: "On their way they were intercepted by Mujahedin or Mujahed who separated all young persons and returned them back to Bikosi." Do you agree that this confirms yet again that Mujahedins are those who separated the group and who took them up to Bikosi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: There is nothing in this translation of this article which I would like to confirm or challenge. This is a translation, again, which was not done by a professional translator. It was our secretary. The way it reads, I think you are correct in interpreting what is being read. But then again, I would rather not interpret a translation of an article.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness ZO. Could you confirm, however, that the four recollections of the events in Maljine that we discussed this morning talked about the involvement of Mujahedin taking people up to Bikosi?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This I can confirm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, in this report also, Witness ZO, the main part of the article refers to an article in Vjesnik - I'm not sure if my pronunciation is right - but it includes a report apparently given to this paper by the Christian Information Service. I refer you to the second page at the first line, where it says: "Some 70 lives beyond redemption," and then the first paragraph. Did you, Witness ZO, have any contacts or any information which was provided to you by the Christian Information Service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I cannot recall such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, again I have made a mistake. I don't know which of the two names that I've just mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can this name be redacted from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry. I think the document should be taken off the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It is not necessary to have the document on the ELMO. I just ask you to look at it in this paragraph. The only question I want to ask you with this is: You recognise that this is a report, or at least what it appears to be, concerning an investigation in the villages of the Brajkovici parish. Can you confirm that you never received the real report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you confirm that you did not speak to any members of this commission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can't remember speaking to any member of this commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this report was, at least according to information we have, was drafted by a Bosnian of Croat origin only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No, I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you are not able to check whether by reading a name you could see whether someone was a Bosnian Muslim or a Bosnian Croat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No. I lack this skill.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But is it something that could have been important for you in treating this document, to know that this report was done only by Bosnian Croats and not with any Bosnian Muslim? Could that be a factor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That could have been a factor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recognise the two members of this commission which were referred to you by the ECMM monitor from Zenica, Mr. Huet, and that you now know that both of these persons testified before this Chamber? You recognise those two names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you did not speak to them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you did not go back on this topic to Mr. Huet from the ECMM, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No, I don't think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you sent a document to Geneva, and I ask you to refer to the first page where it appears that someone who received this document in Geneva on the 20th of July said: "It looks like a propaganda and information branch of Catholic Church here."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then the other comment below, where it says that "On 22 July he called back and said it was a reliable source on previous incidents." Do you also recognise this comment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No. Seemingly this was a comment which was made by someone in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you don't know who "MF" is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I have a guess, a colleague with initials of MF. There was such colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would be in Geneva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Would be in Geneva at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So who was he referring to when he was saying "he," if the drafter of this document is yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This would be an interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In terms of -- is it possible that when he was saying "he called back," is it possible, given that you are the drafter of this document, that he was referring to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall calling in Geneva and saying that this was indeed a reliable source on previous incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in fact you confirm what you said to my colleague this morning that you thought that this specific piece of newspaper was irresponsible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I think I was referring to this article, maybe not, because I remember sending another translation of another article in Vjesnik, which referred to another incident which was completely unfounded. I think that was a different article.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if I refer quickly, Witness ZO, to one of your reports that we were given, where you state something concerning Croatian media.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Mm-hm. [Defence counsel confer]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I will, Witness ZO, simply read to you what is in your -- in one of your reports that we have, where it is mentioned, paragraph 2: "The instigatory role of the Croatian press needs to be studied and condemned. Absolutely unfounded reports of Vjesnik, not speaking of a less reputable media about public hangings in Zenica or of the ratio of distribution of food as 3 to 1 in favour of Muslims call an ordinary brain-washed Croat, especially from Herceg-Bosna, to revenge. This is at least an irresponsible journalism and it can also be qualified as incitement of hatred and provocation." Would you recognise these words as being yours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, one last question with respect to this specific incident: There was a -- you are not aware, or correct me if you are aware, that while this investigation which you were made aware of by the newspaper, you did not request any information nor obtain any concerning a real investigation which was triggered and which involved investigating judge, members of the 3rd Corps of the army, and other people, and that a real investigation was conducted into these allegations or part of these allegations? Do you recall any of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't recall having been informed at any stage about what you refer as "real investigation."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to inform you that the document in question - and this is for the sake of the transcript --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, let me go on. But first I just need to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am told that I have miscalculated and that we have used up our time. I think my colleague used up an hour and 30, so I thought I had 2 hours and 15 minutes for both Defence teams. I need another 45 minutes, in fact, Mr. President. I thought I would need 2 hours and that I would leave my colleagues 15 minutes. It's an error I made. I thought my colleague had taken an hour and a half, but that was my mistake, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time would the other Defence team need?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would only need a short time, no longer than five minutes, if at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So as you have said, you've used up more time than you had. We need to make our second break now, and we'll resume at five to 1.00. In the meantime, we will make a few calculations and tell you how much time you still have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before we give the floor to Defence, there are two minor issues I would like to raise. According to the calculations we have made, Mr. Bourgon, you have 30 minutes and not 45. This is necessary in particular in order to be able to adjourn at the time scheduled. And the second issue I would like to mention is you mentioned document DH156, which concerns a report on events that took place in Susanj and Ovnak, and you gave us the impression that the report concerns Maljine. This concerns page 2 and Maljine is not concerned. The Trial Chamber would like to say that this document doesn't concern the events that occurred in Maljine but only those that occurred in Susanj, and the events in Susanj have been referred to in the press article that were translated and sent to Geneva by the witness. Having said that, you may take the floor for the 30 minutes that you still have.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If I gave the Trial Chamber the impression that my remarks concerned the document mentioned and that they concerned Maljine, I apologise. My purpose was to establish a link between the investigation carried out in Susanj which was an official one, and to compare it with an investigation carried out by an unknown commission which was composed of Bosnian Croats and was also published in the media. This is what I wanted to say. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] Witness ZO, we have 30 minutes left, and I would like to focus on some specific question. Could you confirm that when we had our conversation yesterday you mentioned that there was -- it was common to receive allegations of atrocities; that in fact you were receiving such allegations to the rate of almost two per day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: During the periods where fighting was especially active, yes, that sometimes was the case. Allegations came at this rate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you confirm that very often those allegation proved to be not true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if I give you just one example in which you were personally involved. There was an allegation of a public hanging of Bosnian Croats in front of the Catholic church in Zenica. You were able to confirm, both from Father Stipan and the mayor of Zenica, that this event actually never took place.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like to provide you with some documents which I can -- which we will look at together for the remainder of the time of my cross-examination. I have two documents, one which includes six documents put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have two documents, Mr. President. The first one is a single document dated the 17th of August, 1993, and the second one is a bundle of seven documents, and we have numbered the documents from 1 to 7. We have copies for the Judges and for the witness, and these copies have been numbered. [In English] Can I ensure that the witness has received one of the copies with the tabs so that we can proceed more quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness ZO, I would like to refer you to the single document which you have received. This is a memorandum addressed to Mr. Stoltenberg, who is the special representative of the Secretary-General, from the senior officer on humanitarian affairs. And the subject is "Your inquiry on 16th August regarding alleged BiH atrocities against Croat population." Can you confirm, Witness ZO, that this is one of the documents which you forwarded to Zenica -- sorry, to Geneva as part of your report on 7 October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we would like to tender this document into evidence at -- a little later. The witness has recognised this document. He said that he received it and he forwarded it to Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... Witness ZO, to paragraph 2, where it is said: "It appears that Mr. Boban's claim is at least on some account inaccurate and that UNHCR is aware of only one case of massacre of four Croats in April in Miletici, which was believed to have been done by foreign elements. UNHCR is inclined to believe that although looting and burning of houses do occur, it is not likely that the BiH army has committed extreme atrocities against Croat civilians, as claimed by Mr. Boban." Do you recall having read these comments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me move on, Witness ZO, with the second trip you made to Central Bosnia, and you mentioned to me yesterday that this was from the 23rd to the 25th of September and that the aim of this trip was to observe the situation in several places including Zenica, Stari Vitez, Travnik and of course Maljine. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that, although the trip was in fact longer, but in the central -- in the area of the Lasva Valley, I stayed for two or three days in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you confirm that on the 23rd of September you had meetings in Zenica in the following order: The ECMM mission, the mayor, Spahic, the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, Mr. Merdan, and then Father Stipan, in this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you were never alone for these meetings and that you were accompanied by a Lieutenant Colonel Koet and a Lieutenant Albers - that is in your statement - and yesterday you also mentioned to me that you were accompanied by two members of the ECMM as well as Randy Rhodes, from the civil affairs section. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: It is correct. That's what I told you yesterday. But after straining my memory a bit more, I can now tell that I was mistaken, that there were no ECMM personnel accompanying me to these meetings, that two military officers were in fact from the BH command. I should have made this confusion in my mind, because we've met at the ECMM -- I think we've met in the ECMM office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If I recall your meeting with the mayor, Spahic, would you confirm - and I'm just paraphrasing from one of your reports - that he basically told you, "Human rights are always violated during the war but we have nothing to hide," and that, "In 1991, there were 145.000 people who lived in Zenica, and now there are about 197.000 people, 48.000 of whom are refugees and displaced persons"? Would that ...?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That would be natural for Mr. Mayor, to discuss the demographic picture of this location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you recall the mayor mentioning to you that "Not a single church has been intentionally destroyed in the municipality and that those two which were damaged as a result of the hostilities were repaired at the expense of the municipality"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can in fact confirm this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also recall the mayor telling you that "There were no organised expulsions, that there were no camps, and that prisoners of war were detained in the old city prison, KP Dom, treated humanely and now have now been exchanged"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This would be a natural thing for the mayor to tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you confirm that after your visit you forwarded a letter to the mayor asking for some information on measures that he was taking to take care of criminal matters in his city?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that the mayor answered your letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Now I've seen this letter referred to in the document you distributed, and I can of course confirm that such letter was in fact received.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you turn, Witness ZO, please, to tab number 6 in the second document given to you, which appears to be a letter dated 22 October addressed to someone whom you may know and that this letter is signed -- or at least bears the signature block of the Mayor Spahic from Zenica. Do you recall having ever seen this letter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I recall having seen this letter, although what we have here is again a translation, and I don't see original to the letter itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And by reading the contents, do you recall that this would be the proper contents? I know it's a long letter, but does it appear to be the same letter that you have received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Defence would request that this letter be tendered into evidence. It's under tab 6, and it has been provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... To a meeting you had with Mr. Merdan. Can you confirm that Mr. Merdan began the meeting by a lengthy statement concerning the necessity to develop an effective and a disciplined army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And talking about your meeting with Mr. Merdan, would it be right to say that he also mentioned to you that "The army abides by all international treaties and norms and assists all the international humanitarian organisations and that army laws and regulations are strict but some bad individuals do cause some problems and the army will soon throw away all those who do not respect the law and don't obey orders"? Do you recall such a conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I do recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You also recall that when talking about Maljine, contrary to what he said, he did not say that he was aware of allegations but he basically informed you that there was, in Maljine, there may be some mass graves in Maljine and that he could not issue you a permission to go there because it was the policy to have the local commander authorise such visit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This was the conversation between me and Mr. Merdan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he never denied the possibility of an occurrence happening in Maljine, but he did tell you that no civilians were killed in Maljine, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he also told you that it was normal after a combat operation to mop up the land and then to pay respect to the soldiers who had fallen during battle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can't remember anything about respect, and I think the term he used was translated to me was "to sanitise the area."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: And to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You are correct, Witness ZO. "Pay respect" was my own wording, which simply meant to take care of the bodies which have been picked up. Could we agree on this interpretation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I would agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall also Mr. Merdan as saying that the area controlled by 3rd Corps "not a single Croat village had been burned and not a single church destroyed"? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you also recall that when answering your question on Mujahedin, he said that "There are no Mujahedin units in the BiH army but there are volunteers from a number of countries including some Westerners. They came to fight back modern fascism and all of them are required to obey orders and to respect the laws of the army"? Do you recall this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This in fact is what Mr. Merdan told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next meeting you had was with Father Stipan, and Father Stipan -- I asked you yesterday if you were aware that Father Stipan was under the protection of the army and that he had a laissez-passer to go around. Am I correct in saying that you cannot confirm this but what you did tell me was that he at least acted as he was not hiding, not scared, spoke openly, without fear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Father Stipan did mention to you the issue of Maljine, but according to him this had been done by Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Father Stipan also confirmed that there were no major problems in conducting religious services in Zenica and that people were not afraid to go to church.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And he also confirmed the issue that the church had been repaired at the expense of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: It's also in my report, and that's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Father Stipan did not mention to you that in August he had visited Maljine along with a delegation from ECMM and Mr. Merdan, according -- the alleged atrocities. He never mentioned that to you, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: He he didn't mention this to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to refer to P164 under tab 1. I would just like to refer to this document which is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... In those that I gave to you now but it is included in the tab number 1. It is a report that is from ECMM saying that Father Stipan, accompanied by Mr. Merdan and ECMM monitors, did visit Maljine in August. But you can confirm, Witness ZO, that Merdan never informed you -- sorry, that Father Stipan did not inform you of this visit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you also confirm, Witness ZO, that when you met with Merdan - and that was before you met Father Stipan - you did not request from him any information as to any investigation being taken -- being handled by the Bosnian army into the events in Maljine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can't remember posing him such a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next meeting you had, Witness ZO, with a gentleman called Salko Beba. And you can confirm that he was not happy with the fact that Merdan had issued instructions to you that local commanders were to authorise visits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I cannot say that this was an instruction from Merdan to me. It was just what he told me, that this was not his policy to issue such permissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So Mr. Salko Beba was on a different policy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: He was definitely on a different wavelength.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you had a good lunch with Mr. Salko Beba, during which you drank a lot of very good rekija. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I don't think that I drank a lot of good rekija, but I think the rekija I drank was good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Merdan only drank. But Witness ZO, when you had this meeting with Mr. Salko Beba, would I be right to say that he mentioned to you that anyone who plunders and harasses Croats, if he would catch any such people, the punishment would be immediate and painful because "he who comes at night to steal from an old Croat woman, even if he is my brother, I will order my people to beat him up"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That's what --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember such wordings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you also remember that when speaking about Mujahedin he claimed that a lot of people in Bosnia and Herzegovina did not want to live in a fundamentalist Bosnia? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I need to bring you back, Witness ZO, to line 22 of page 85, where my question says: "Maybe Mr. Merdan only drank." So I just would like the make a correction. And what I told you is maybe only Mr. Beba drank. That would be in line with your -- of course your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Because Mr. Merdan was not there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: He was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it also fair to say that he said this the main role of the Mujahedin was that of brainwashers and levers of influence on personnel? Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you also recall that he mentioned to you that "Muj," to use the words that there in the report, "are not united. Some of them fight in regular troops and obey orders and others really set their own agenda"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you also recall that when you proceeded to Guca Gora you were there with Mr. Beba at his suggestion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you had nevertheless to negotiate access to the area with the local commander, as you mentioned earlier this morning on page 30?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You nevertheless -- you were with Mr. Beba but you had to ask permission to gain access to the local commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct. And Mr. Beba was helpful in indicating the right person to me and even suggested in which terms I could approach this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Guca Gora, you did not find anything, and you proceeded to Maljine.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: What do you mean I didn't find anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There was no prison, as you say, in your report, or no one being detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I didn't find any evidence of a detention centre being located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you did see that the church was under the protection of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I've seen there some military personnel, and they told me that they were protecting the church, and I saw nothing which could contradict that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you then proceeded to Guca Gora. And when you saw those two patches of fresh earth that was there, you did not believe what the soldiers told you, that this was dated from a long time back.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct. But this was in Maljine, not in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry, in Maljine. And in Maljine, the person who offered you a shovel to dig was one of your escorts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: No. He was the one who was already there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if in your report it says that it was one of your escorts, which one would be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That it was the one who was there before I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if I -- that when you were in Maljine, you were informed that some people might have been buried in another area 2 kilometres from there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: That was the information I received previously, I think from Father Stipan, that there is a mass grave but it's not really at the site of the execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, if we go on to following this visit. Then -- I'd like to refer you to some letters which are in the document in front of you. You can confirm that at your suggestion, or at least you had a role to play in a letter that was forwarded by the Special Rapporteur to the president of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like you -- to refer you to document number 2, or tab number 2 in your document, which is a letter addressed from the commander of the army to the 3rd Corps Command, and that -- would you by the reading of this letter, which talks about the president of the Presidency having received a letter from the Special Rapporteur, would you agree that this is following the letter received to which you had a role to play?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I would very much agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would like to note to you that this is a letter that is already in the record at Exhibit P171. I would now like you to turn to tab number 3, where it says "Request for submission of data." And this is a letter dated 17 October. Can you confirm that this letter is also a follow-up to the letter from Mr. Mazowiecki?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I would agree to that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, in you look at the original letter, the one in the Bosnian language, there is a signature there but it is signed on behalf of Enver Hadzihasanovic, commander of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a contested document because we would like to have a witness for this letter. Given that the witness is here before the Trial Chamber now, he could explain where this letter comes from, and after the witness's testimony I would like this letter to be tendered into evidence, so we would no longer be contesting it. Nevertheless, Mr. President, one of the questions raised by the Defence concerns the signature, and we stand by our position with regard to the signature in this document. But we would like this letter to be admitted into evidence, so we will no longer be contesting it. But this is what we will do after the testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... In this document. Now, this tab number 4 is a letter addressed from the 3rd Corps to the Supreme Command of the armed forces. And again, can you confirm that this letter is the follow-up to the investigation which was done within the 3rd Corps and this is being now reported to the army headquarters? Without going through the contents, would you agree that this is a follow-up to what is being done within the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: This certainly looks to me like this is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I note for the record, Mr. President, that this letter bears the exhibit number P174.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness ZO, I now take you to tab number 5, and this is a letter dated 23 October, which is addressed from the defence of the republic, and that is the office of the commander, and it's addressed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. And again, this is the follow-up where the Minister of Foreign Affairs is being informed as to what investigation took place within the 3rd Corps following the letter of Mr. Mazowiecki. Would you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Again, this very much looks like this is the case to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I note for the record that this letter bears number P175.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I ask you to turn to tab number 7. Would you recognise, Witness ZO, that this is a typical report done by the Economic and Social Council, and that is the Special Rapporteur's report, and that this one bears the date 21 February 1994? Do you recognise this type of document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Of course I do, with one small correction. This is not the report done by the Economic and Social Council but rather to the Economic and Social council. That's why it bears the name of the Economic and Social Council. This is the report which on a routine basis provided by Special Rapporteur and other mechanisms of the commission on human rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness ZO. I just draw your attention to paragraph 22, where in the report the Special Rapporteur mentions the conclusions of the government with respect to his letter which was forwarded, and that you were the initiator. I do not have time to go through more. I would simply now to conclude draw your attention to the conclusion in your report which you prepared on 4 October, and I would simply quote you to confirm that these were indeed your conclusions, where it is stated: "My overall impression is that the BiH government and the army do not pursue the policy of ethnic cleansing of Croats in those territories under their control which I was able to visit." Would you confirm this wording as being from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: These are my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And also, where it says that "Many Croats who fled their homes in the beginning of the fighting did that as a result of corresponding propaganda in which of course the Mujahedin factor is of prominent importance but under specific orders by the HVO"? Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Yes, these are also my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you also confirm that you said "Croat minorities in Zenica and Bugojno, absent Vitez, seemingly are better off than Muslim minority in the HVO-held pocket of Lasva Valley and Kiseljak, Kresevo"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can also confirm that these are my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness ZO. I have no further questions. I thank you very much. We had to go a bit quick for the last part in order to allow me to finish within 30 minutes. [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to thank the Trial Chamber for their indulgence, and I would also like to repeat that it was my mistake when I calculated the time we had. And once we have finished with the examination of this witness, we will be asking for this document to be tendered into it. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura for this witness. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Re-examination on the part to have Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There's no questions in re-examination, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the documents are concerned, the Defence has given us certain documents, some of them with numbers. As a matter of fact, there are two documents which were contested; they are tab 3 and now the Defence no longer contests this document. And the Defence has asked for these documents on tab 6 to be admitted into evidence. This is a letter from the Municipality of Zenica to the witness. So these are the documents that you want to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, but there are also other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, there are three documents. Before I give the floor to the Prosecution to hear their observations, just an observation on my part regarding the documents: You have said to the witness that on the 17th of October the commander of the 3rd Corps sent a request to the operations group to submit information on the events in Maljine. I observe that we have not been provided with the response by the operations group. In addition to that, in the letter that Mr. Merdan sent in reply to the request received on the 17th of October, it says your document dated 17 of October -- your letter, rather, of 20th of October. Here we have a document dated the 17th, but again we do not have a document dated the 20th, which was supposed to be drafted by Mr. Delic. So there are two documents missing. You have not submitted those documents. Maybe they exist somewhere else, but they are not in the bundle that you have provided us with. You wanted to show something with this bundle, but we have to state that some documents are missing from the bundle. This was my observation, and now I would like to hear the remarks on the part to have Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with respect to the third document at tab -- the document at tab 3 that the Defence had previously contested and which now they seek to tender, might I suggest that because the Prosecution had first tendered that document into evidence and in light of the Chamber's ruling with respect to the documents that were tendered through General Reinhardt by the Defence, that that be given a Prosecution number. We have no objection obviously to that document going into evidence, as it's one which we initially proposed for admission into evidence. With respect to the document at tab 6, we have no objection to that document being admitted into evidence. It's unclear to me what the Defence wanted to do with the letter addressed to Mr. Stoltenberg, whether that was to be tendered or whether that was just to be marked. Let me leave that for the Defence. With respect to the documents that Your Honour highlighted, which would appear to be some missing documents in the chain, I am unable at this point to provide any additional clarification. However we will certainly check amongst the documents which are on the contested document list to determine whether any of those documents in fact are pieces of this puzzle. We will make that inquiry, Mr. President. Perhaps we can advise you as to that tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Mundis, we would kindly request you to do that. And now back to the documents, tab 3, tab 6, no problems there. The Prosecution has some reservations about the documents sent by the United Nations to Geneva.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the document that being discussed now, the Defence would like this document to be tendered into evidence, not only because the witness has recognised it but also this is a document that he had in his possession, this is a document that he used in his work, and he personally sent it to Geneva together with some other documents. The witness has also recognised the contents of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Mr. Registrar, can we have three numbers, first for the document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we agreed that the numbers may be retained, the numbers by the Prosecution, because the Prosecution tendered these documents into evidence first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Let's first deal with the documents sent to the United Nations, then the document which is at tab 6, and finally the document at tab 3. And then we will address the other issues.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the information report dated 17th of August, 1993 gets the exhibit number DH179, under seal. The English translation of a letter from Spahic dated 22nd of October, 1993 and which was tendered as tab 6 here gets the exhibit number DH180, under seal. The document from the 3rd Corps gets the exhibit number P111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. You have all recorded these three numbers. We still have a document that was "Instruction to the Muslim Fighter." This instruction or this manual has been given to the witness. Would you like this document to be tendered into evidence or not? Would you like the "Instruction to the Muslim Fighter" to be tendered into evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution certainly would like that tendered into evidence if Your Honours think it would be helpful for the issues that you have to ultimately address. I assume that my learned colleagues will object to that, but if Your Honours believe that it is helpful, we would certainly offer that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards this document which has been translated into English, which was drafted in 1993 in Zenica, which cost 50.000-something in local currency - we don't know what was the currency there at the time. We can see who the publisher is, who the author is, and the document has been recognised by the witness. In this document, we can see a number of chapters concerning religious issues, amongst which there are also chapters concerning prisoners of war and war booty. Mr. Dixon, obviously you have some objections to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour will be aware that this was a document which we indicated we did require a witness for, because it was only marked for identification initially as a soldier from the 7th Brigade was not able to recognise it when the Prosecution sought to introduce it through him. That was Witness BA back in December of last year. Your Honours, we would continue to maintain our objection and require a witness who can identify the document. All this witness was able to do in his testimony was -- he was able to identify a few pages in English, not the original in B/C/S, and certainly not the entire exhibit. He was able to indicate that he got a few pages as part of his briefing from the UN. We would have no objection to those pages going in as documents that he received and recognised, but we would object to the whole document going in on the basis that he wasn't able to recognise the entire document and wasn't able to do so in its official language. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. The witness is before us. I would like to ask him a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document which you have been provided with, you said that it was provided to you. Who was it who provided you with it? A civilian or a soldier? Who was it that you got this document from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: I can't remember. I only remember that this has been provided to me in the premises of HQ of BH command in Kiseljak. And there were meetings all the time and papers have been presented to us attention or given to us. I cannot remember from whose hands I received these several pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whoever gave this document to you, it was on the army premises, so I suppose this person could not have been a civilian, could it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Being BH command, of course, the predominant group of occupants were military --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: -- but there were quite a number of civilians also working for UNHCR or civil affairs, so there were not -- it was not the case that it would be exclusive military personnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give you the floor in a minute. This document that you were given, according to what you remember, was that a document that was original and bound, or was that a photocopy of the original document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: These were several sheets of photocopies. It was not the original text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why were you given this document in the first place? You're not a soldier. You remember not a member of the army. Why were you given this document? Do you remember what reasons were given to you when you were being given this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Since I can't remember the circumstances under which this document has been provided to me, it's difficult for me to guess the reasons. But people knew that we were after relevant information, and I would say that information which was contained on these several sheets of paper was relevant to my mandate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to make sure of something. I don't know whether the witness could confirm this, but concerning questions of BH command, this concerns the UNPROFOR headquarters, not the headquarters of one of the parties. These are the UN headquarters where we can see both civilians and members of the military, but not people from the BH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this was the UNPROFOR headquarters. It wasn't the BH army. This document was provided to you by someone from UNPROFOR headquarters in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: Absolutely so. And this would have been impossible that somebody from the BH army would have given this to me in the premises of UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But given that this document was on sale. In theory it was on sale, because there was a price; you could have bought it in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS ZO
utterances.text: To my surprise, if I understand your words, I understand that this was in public sale. This fact has never been indicated to me and this has not been explained to me when these several sheets together were given to me -- these several sheets of paper were given to me. As I have said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will deliberate about this issue, and we will see what should be done with regard to this document. Unless Mr. Mundis has any other clarifications to provide, we could adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just briefly. It's the Prosecution's understanding that the number on page 44 of the document, the 50.000 number, refers to the print run; that is, the number of copies of this document that were produced and not to the cost of the document. I simply draw that to the Chamber's attention in case there's any confusion. Our interpretation, Mr. President, is that this was a document or a booklet or publication that 350.000 copies were printed up. I just want to avoid any possible confusion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we note that the number "50.000" doesn't represent the price, because I would have consulted the B/C/S line. I had a look at the line in B/C/S. But as I don't know the B/C/S language, I thought it was the price. But you are telling us that it is the print run. Yes, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Very briefly. There's just one further matter that I wish to draw to Your Honours' attention in deliberating this matter, and that is this witness indicated in his examination-in-chief that he was not sure of the status of this document, it's not clear to him, and that he couldn't deduce that it was a book of the Bosnian army. In our submission, that is very relevant information because the Prosecution seeks to introduce this document to support its allegation in the indictment that 20.000 copies -- not 50.000 but 20.000 copies of this booklet were distributed within the 3rd Corps area of responsibility, and it's for the purpose of proving that point that this exhibit is sought to be introduced, I would take it. And if the witness cannot give any evidence as to the origin of the booklet and what its status was, we would submit that he's not the appropriate witness to introduce the booklet and that there are future witness who is may be able to do that. I'm grateful, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Given that we have almost completed the examination of this witness -- Unless Mr. Bourgon would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to address the issue raised by the Trial Chamber concerning the missing documents. Mr. President, we are actively searching for these documents. We have found one additional document. We found it this night by using the electronic search of the Prosecution. We found a letter addressed by Mr. Izetbegovic to the chief of the Main Staff of the army. So this is a fragment of the overall picture. We are looking for these documents. The one that we have presented today -- we have referred to today are in our possession -- are the ones that are in possession but we will do everything we can to find the documents in order to provide you with a full picture of the events. But there are other steps that we will have to take and that we will take in the course of the following week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness, for having come to testify here. You have answered all the questions put to you, and we wish you a good trip home. I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have a few more seconds. Mr. Mundis, a witness is scheduled for tomorrow, and there's the transcript of an audiotape. Can you inform the Trial Chamber of how you intend to proceed, because there are a number of possibilities. The audiotape could perhaps be listened to in totality; we could listen to the first five minutes of it. How did you intend to present the witness -- to proceed with the witness and with this audiotape? And how did you intend to tender this transcript into evidence? For the time being, this is a contested document, and I'm asking you this question so as not the waste any time tomorrow on technical issues that can be easily solved. And then we will be in a position to know in advance how we will proceeding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The full audiotape that was presented by the witness to the Prosecution runs approximately 32 minutes. It's the Prosecution's intention, and I have explained this -- or mentioned this to the Defence earlier this morning - was to play certain excerpts, a few minutes of that audiotape, in open court so that the witness could properly authenticate the tape. We would then be seeking to tender into evidence the transcript of the audiotape. And I can tell my learned colleagues that in fact that transcript is the only document that will be used in respect to the witness who is here for tomorrow. So we would propose to play a short excerpt or perhaps two excerpts from the tape so that the witness can properly identify and authenticate what's happening and then of course show him the transcript, have him verify that the transcript in fact matches the tape. And then we'll tender that transcript into evidence. If Your Honours would prefer to hear the full 32 minutes, we can happily do that, but our intention was only to play one or perhaps two excerpts from the tape, in order to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to Defence to address this issue, how much time did you think it would take you to conduct your examination-in-chief of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, I'll be meeting with the witness this afternoon after lunch, so it's a bit difficult. I would not anticipate the direct examination lasting more than one hour. I would anticipate that by the first technical break I should be finished, or very close to being finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you know, the Trial Chamber is always concerned when a witness is called on Friday, because we're always worried about obliging this witness to remain over the weekend in order to continue with the witness's testimony on Monday. This is why the Trial Chamber likes to know in advance whether this is a risk. As far as the technical means are concerned, as far as the idea of having the witness recognise certain excerpts without listening to the entire tape, Mr. Bourgon, what would your position be?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution has informed us of this procedure, and we have no objection to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have dealt with all the issues, and we will now adjourn. I will see everyone tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 21st day of May, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.54 p.m.,
